findings.title: SPX Monte Carlo is not an Ito scheme: sigma is taken from X_{t+dt} and multiplied by the same shock, so S is not a martingale. The published 2.34 vp SPX fit comes from this bias
findings.description: _run_mc_paths first advances X,Y with Z1 (lines 404-405). It then computes sigma from the updated state and uses that sigma times the same Z1 in the log-price increment (414-415). The integrand is therefore not adapted: the scheme converges to a backward-Ito integral that carries an extra quadratic-covariation drift eps*g0*p'(Z)*(theta*sx+(1-theta)*sy). That drift is O(dt) per step, O(1) in total, and does not shrink as the grid is refined. Consequences: (1) E[S_T] is not equal to the forward. (2) Deep-ITM calls price below intrinsic, which is a no-arbitrage violation, so their IVs come back NaN. (3) At the stored calibrated parameters the put skew comes out inverted. Every stored Quintic parameter was fitted to this biased pricer. At the same parameters a correct Ito pricer gives an SPX RMSE of about 4 vp, above the Heston baseline's 3.83, instead of the published 2.34 vp. The dashboard text 'Quote the SPX-leg RMSE (2.34 vp) as the real fit quality' and 'captures steep SPX left skew' are therefore artifacts of the bug. g0 is also evaluated at t_mid while Z is at t_{k+1}, which is a small extra inconsistency.
findings.evidence:
All runs in the scratch copy (PYTHONPATH=.).

(a) Martingale test with _run_mc_paths, stored params, 200k paths:
- T=0.0384: E[S_T/F] = 1.00137 ± 0.00012 (z = +11.3)
- T=0.1808: 0.99231 ± 0.00025 (z = -31)
- T=0.4877: 0.97799 ± 0.00041 (z = -54)
- T=0.9863: 0.95726 ± 0.00058 (z = -74)

The test-file fixture params show the same bias (λx=35, θ=0.94, ε=-0.75, flat ξ=0.04): T=1.0 gives 0.96318 ± 0.00043.

(b) Same model with left-point Ito (sigma from X_t, then advance): T=0.986 gives 0.99990 ± 0.00085; T=0.488 gives 0.99991 ± 0.00059. Both are martingales.

(c) SPX RMSE vs market for the 54-option calibration set:
- repo pricer, 10k paths, seed 42 (as published): 2.343
- repo scheme, fresh 200k paths: 2.616
- Ito, 50 steps/yr: 3.964
- Ito, 252 steps/yr: 4.079
- Ito, 2520 steps/yr: 4.179

Max per-option difference between the repo pricer and the correct pricer is 5.67 vp. Per-expiry mean IV at T=0.986: repo 0.2151, Ito 0.2695, market 0.2230.

(d) Put skew, T=0.4877, K/S = 0.90 / 0.95 / 0.98 / 1.00:
- market (mid): 0.2608 / 0.2361 / 0.2213 / 0.2113
- repo pricer: 0.1883 / 0.2079 / 0.2141 / 0.2169 (inverted skew)
- K/S = 0.85: repo pricer returns NaN (price below intrinsic)
findings.proposed_fix:
Rewrite _run_mc_paths as a left-point Ito scheme:
1. At step k, compute sigma_k = g0(t_k)*p(Z_{t_k}) from the pre-update state, with g0 using fv(t_k) and var_Z(t_k).
2. Update log S with sigma_k and the step's Brownian increments.
3. Only then advance X and Y.

Simulate (I_X, I_Y, ΔW) jointly and exactly as a 3-D Gaussian with:
- Var I_X = (1-e^{-2λx dt})/(2λx); Var I_Y likewise
- Cov(I_X, I_Y) = (1-e^{-(λx+λy)dt})/(λx+λy)
- Cov(I_X, ΔW) = (1-e^{-λx dt})/λx; Cov(I_Y, ΔW) likewise
- Var ΔW = dt

Use the Cholesky factor of that covariance, and the independent W⊥ increment for the orthogonal part. Remove the max(·,0) floor (see the separate finding). Use 252 steps/yr with a minimum of 100, matching the authors' reference code. Optionally add the reference implementation's conditional-MC (Romano–Touzi mixing) with the timer-option control variate.

I prototyped this. It gives E[S/F] = 0.99946 ± 0.00087 at T=0.986, and IV at K=6925 of 0.2669 / 0.2676 / 0.2677 for 50 / 252 / 1000 steps/yr.

Then recalibrate and republish the RMSE; fixing the VIX-leg performance finding makes this cheap.

Tests:
- a martingale test, |E[S_T/F]-1| < 4 s.e. at T ∈ {0.25, 1} for both the fixture and the calibrated params;
- a step-convergence test, IV(252 steps/yr) vs IV(1000 steps/yr) < 0.3 vp;
- a no-arbitrage test, deep-ITM call price ≥ discounted intrinsic.

findings.title: VIX-option target IVs are vendor Black-Scholes IVs on spot VIX, not Black-76 on the VIX forward. The 17.5 vp figure is measured against a wrong target, and 70% of it comes from 5 near-ATM calls
findings.description:
_prepare_vix_options compares model Black-76 IVs, computed with the model's own E[VIX_T] as forward, against the stored `implied_vol` column, which comes from yfinance. On 2026-03-24 those vendor IVs are Black-Scholes IVs with spot VIX (26.95) as the underlying. VIX options are priced off the VIX future, which put-call parity puts at about 23.4–24.4 that day. As a result the stored put IVs are inflated (0.6–1.5) and the call IVs deflated (0.17–0.32) at the same strikes.

Other selection problems in the same function:
- 'ATM' is defined by a hard-coded spot_vix_proxy = 20.0 (line 268) while VIX was 26.95.
- There is no call/put or OTM filter, so the set is 35 puts and 5 calls.
- There is no liquidity filter: open_interest is 0 on every row and volume is 1–5 on many rows.

The published 17.53 vp is dominated by the 5 calls whose target IVs are artifacts. The dashboard's explanation ('residual is in the VIX-smile wings… far-OTM VIX calls') is false. The fitted strikes are only 18–23, and no far-OTM VIX call is in the set.
findings.evidence:
Reproduced the pickle exactly with the current code and DB: VIX-options RMSE = 17.5297 vp (n = 40), SPX = 2.3427, VIX futures = 0.001147.

Put-call parity forwards from the stored mids (r = 4.5%) by expiry:
- 2026-04-15: 24.41
- 05-19: 23.68
- 06-17: 23.44
- 07-22: 23.55

Two IVs compared on the 2026-06-17 chain: the stored vendor IV and my re-inversion of the mid as Black–Scholes on spot VIX (26.95):

| option | stored vendor IV | BS on spot VIX (26.95) | Black-76 on PCP forward |
|---|---|---|---|
| P20 | 0.985 | 1.009 | 0.775 |
| C25 | 0.482 | 0.453 | 0.929 |
| P25 | 1.225 | 1.259 | 0.943 |

The spot-VIX re-inversion lands close to the vendor numbers, which is what shows the vendor used spot VIX. With the parity forward, the call and put at K=25 agree (0.929 vs 0.943).

On the 40 calibration rows:
- RMSE between the stored target and the correct Black-76 target: 24.2 vp
- Published metric split: puts n=35, RMSE 10.27 vp, 30% of the squared error; calls n=5, RMSE 41.47 vp, 70% of the squared error
- Example call rows (T, K): stored target vs model IV: (0.233, 23C) 0.3189 vs 0.8576; (0.655, 22C) 0.1690 vs 0.5477
- Model vs the correct Black-76 target: 16.40 vp with the repo's inversion, 15.19 vp with proper discounting
findings.proposed_fix:
Rebuild the VIX-option target from prices:
1. Per expiry, estimate the forward F as the median of K + e^{rT}(C−P) over the 3 strikes with the smallest |C−P|. Use CBOE VX settlements instead when they are available.
2. Keep OTM quotes only: puts for K < F, calls for K ≥ F.
3. Liquidity filters: bid > 0, (ask−bid)/mid < 0.3, volume or open interest > 0.
4. Invert the mids with Black-76 on F.
5. Select strikes on a log-moneyness grid relative to F (for example k ∈ [−0.1, 1.0], as in the authors' demo) instead of |K−20|.
6. Delete spot_vix_proxy.
7. Compare the model's IV at K/F_model to the market IV at the same K/F_mkt, or add a futures leg (see the separate finding).

Re-run and republish, and replace the 'far-OTM wings' sentence with the measured residual decomposition.

Tests:
- a synthetic Black-76 chain round-trips to the input vol within 0.1 vp;
- on the 03-24 chain, call and put Black-76 IVs at the same strike agree within 3 vp.

findings.title: 'VIX futures by construction' is false. The w2 leg does not depend on the parameters, and the model's actual VIX futures miss the market forward by 2.2 pts
findings.description: The 'VIX futures' leg compares _spot_vix(T, ξ0) with the ^VIX9D/^VIX/^VIX3M/^VIX6M index levels. Both sides are functions of the bootstrapped ξ0 and of no model parameter, so the leg adds a constant to the loss and its 'RMSE' (0.0011) only measures bootstrap round-off. What ξ0 matches is the variance-swap term structure (the VIX indices), not VIX futures. The model's real VIX futures price E[VIX_T] (price_vix_futures) is never compared with any market futures quote. When it is compared with the put-call-parity forwards implied by the VIX option chain, it is 0.6–2.6 pts too high at every expiry: the model's VIX convexity is far too small. The dashboard still shows 0.001 in green next to Heston's 0.266 with a negative delta, and README:162 advertises 'VIX futures by-construction'.
findings.evidence:
At the stored params, model E[VIX_T] vs the PCP-implied market forward, by expiry:

| T | model | market |
|---|---|---|
| 0.060 | 25.03 | 24.41 |
| 0.153 | 24.74 | 23.68 |
| 0.233 | 25.85 | 23.44 |
| 0.329 | 26.11 | 23.55 |
| 0.405 | 26.11 | 23.48 |
| 0.482 | 26.11 | 23.57 |
| 0.578 | 26.11 | 23.69 |
| 0.655 | 26.11 | 23.61 |

RMSE = 2.218 pts.

The index leg itself reproduces the inputs regardless of the parameters: _spot_vix(0.0822, fv) = 26.9500 vs ^VIX 26.95; _spot_vix(0.2493) = 26.562 vs 26.56. The leg does not appear in any parameter gradient (code inspection: model_vix = _spot_vix(T_vix, fv), with no params argument).
findings.proposed_fix:
1. Replace the w2 leg with a real futures leg: (price_vix_futures(T, params) − F_mkt(T))², where F_mkt comes from CBOE VX settlements (store them) or, as a fallback, from the VIX-option put-call parity forward. Use the VIX option expiries.
2. Keep the index-term-structure reproduction as a sanity assertion (< 0.01 pts), not as a fit metric.
3. Relabel it on the dashboard as 'ξ0 input reproduction'.
4. Publish the true futures RMSE. Change README:162 to state that ξ0 is bootstrapped from the VIX indices and quote the futures misfit.

Test: price_vix_futures reproduces the market forwards on a synthetic model-generated dataset; the loss changes when the params change and the w2 leg is on.

findings.title: Published Quintic-vs-Heston comparisons use different dates, datasets and metrics, and the baseline JSON cannot be reproduced
findings.description:
There are four separate problems.

(1) The live calibration page computes spx_delta and vix_delta as quintic(2026-03-24) minus d['spx_rmse']. d['spx_rmse'] is the LATEST Heston fit, currently joint_cal_2026-09-11 with only 9 SPX options (the outage-era degenerate fit). The page therefore shows the Quintic as '+2.128 vp' worse than Heston in red. The same-date baseline JSON has Heston at 3.83 vp. The Bates panel (lines 569-596) has the same cross-date bug.

(2) README:77 and the panel's '17.5 vs 37.1 vp (~53% reduction)' compare two different metrics on two different option sets:
- Heston: 14 options, 2 expiries of 91 days or less, strikes 20–38, vega-normalised price error.
- Quintic: 40 options, 8 expiries, strikes 18–23, IV difference.

(3) The panel says Heston's VIX-option leg is 'DISABLED' and in the same breath 'beats Heston's 37.1 vp'.

(4) baseline_2026-03-24.json does not match the current code or data:
- it stores S = 6581.0, the 03-23 close; the DB's 03-24 close is 6556.37;
- it stores rho = −0.95, yet its SPX RMSE (3.8333588958635674) is bit-identical to the Bates pickle's heston_comparison, which records heston_rho = −0.99;
- the current code at the JSON's parameters gives different losses (see evidence).

The JSON is also the NN pricer's training centre (nn_pricer.py:75).
findings.evidence:
Live https://navnoorbawa.me/calibration.html shows: 'SPX IV RMSE (vp) 0.215 | 2.343 | +2.128' and 'VIX Fut RMSE (pts) 0.266 | 0.001 | -0.265'.

joint_cal_2026-09-11.pkl: leg_losses spx 0.2152, vix_fut 0.2664, n_spx_options = 9.

Like-for-like check: the Quintic stored params priced on the Heston calibrator's own 14 VIX options with its own metric (vega-normalised price error) give 26.69 vp. Heston on the same set with current code gives 37.84 vp (JSON: 37.14). That is a 29% reduction, not 53%.

JointCalibrator('2026-03-24') at the JSON parameters:
- rho = −0.95: SPX 2.6694 vp, VIX futures 1.8741
- rho = −0.99: SPX 2.6101 vp
- JSON: 3.8334 / 1.1502

Bates pickle: heston_comparison {'heston_spx_rmse': 3.8333588958635674, 'heston_rho': -0.99}, and n_evals = 0.
findings.proposed_fix:
1. In load_page2, compare the Quintic and Bates panels only with a Heston fit from the same as_of_date. Regenerate a 2026-03-24 Heston fit with the current code and store it with S, r, q, the snapshot date and the code SHA. If none exists, show 'no same-date baseline' instead of a delta.
2. Assert that the dates are equal before computing spx_delta and vix_delta.
3. Recompute both VIX-option numbers on one common, correctly built option set and metric (see the VIX-target finding), and replace '53%' with the measured like-for-like figure.
4. Regenerate baseline_2026-03-24.json from code instead of hand-editing it, then retrain or validate the NN centre.

Test: a dashboard unit test fails when the panel's Heston comparison as_of differs from the Quintic as_of.

findings.title: The 'antithetic' second half uses fresh draws with the sign flipped, so there is no variance reduction and the standard-error formula is wrong once this is fixed
findings.description: price_spx_options_mc calls _run_mc_paths twice with the same RandomState object. The second call (flip=True) draws the NEXT block of normals and negates them, so its paths are independent of the first half, not mirror images. The docstrings ('antithetic variates') and the calibrator's CRN/speed rationale rely on a variance reduction that does not happen. The noise that remains lets DE/L-BFGS fit MC noise: the in-sample RMSE is 2.343, and re-evaluating the same pricer on fresh paths gives 2.616.
findings.evidence:
Correlation between the terminal log-returns of the two halves:
- as coded: T=0.0384 → −0.0075; T=0.4877 → −0.0072
- true antithetic (reset rng, same draws negated): −0.8178 and −0.5278

The SPX RMSE of the same (buggy) pricer at the stored params rises from 2.343 (in-sample CRN, 10k paths, seed 42) to 2.616 (200k fresh paths).
findings.proposed_fix:
Pre-draw Z1 and Z2 of shape (n_steps, half) once and run the path loop on the concatenation [Z, −Z], as the reference gen_bm_path does with np.concatenate((w1, -w1), axis=1). Compute standard errors on pair averages: std(0.5*(dp[:h]+dp[h:]))/sqrt(h).

Test: the corr of the two halves' logS is < −0.3, and the stderr from pair averages is below the iid stderr of the same number of plain paths.

findings.title: VIX-option IV inversion treats the undiscounted model expectation as a discounted price, which biases model IVs by up to 5.6 vp
findings.description: price_vix_option returns E[(VIX_T−K)+], with no discounting. vix_option_implied_vol inverts it against disc*(F N(d1) − K N(d2)) with disc = e^{−rT}, and also uses discounted no-arbitrage bounds. The extra (1−disc) of intrinsic value shows up as time value, so model IVs are inflated, and most of all for the ITM calls that the calibrator uses in place of the OTM puts it is given. Either both sides must be undiscounted, or the model price must be multiplied by disc.
findings.evidence:
Stored params, 22×22 GH quadrature (the reported recipe). Model IV, repo inversion vs proper discounting:
- T=0.6548, K=18: 0.5989 vs 0.5433 (5.6 vp)
- T=0.6548, K=22: 0.5477 vs 0.5204 (2.7 vp)
- T=0.2329, K=20: 0.9009 vs 0.8789 (2.2 vp)

On the 40-row set against the correct Black-76 target: 16.40 vp with the repo inversion, 15.19 vp with discounting.
findings.proposed_fix:
In price_vix_option, return disc*E[...] and document it as a present value. Alternatively, call vix_option_implied_vol with r=0 on undiscounted quantities, as the authors' vec_find_iv_rat(…, r=0.0) does. Compute model puts via parity with the model F rather than inverting ITM calls. Move the scipy.stats import out of black76_call.

Test: a round trip in which a Black-76 price generated at σ=0.8, F=24, T=0.5, r=4.5% inverts back to 0.8 through the same code path as the model.

findings.title: Parameterisation departs from Abi Jaber–Li: α5 is free (a scale-redundant direction), a max(p,0) floor makes the SPX and VIX legs different models, and the fitted point violates the martingale condition with a reversed instantaneous leverage
findings.description:
This finding compares the code with arXiv:2503.14158 and the authors' reference code (github.com/shaunlinz02/two_factor_quintic_ou).

(1) The paper notes that the model is invariant to rescaling p and fixes α5 = 1. The code frees all four α, so the 8-D DE and L-BFGS-B search has an exactly flat direction.

(2) The SPX MC floors σ = max(g0·p, 0). The VIX leg and the g0 normalisation use p². Where p < 0 the two legs therefore price different models, and flipping α → −α leaves the VIX leg unchanged while the SPX vol collapses. The bounds are sign-symmetric, so half of the search box lies in this inconsistent region.

(3) The paper's sufficient condition for S to be a true martingale is α5 > 0 and ρ ≤ 0. The stored fit has α5 = −0.4895 and ε = −0.1823.

(4) At the stored fit, p'(z) has no real root and α1 < 0, so p is decreasing everywhere. The instantaneous spot-vol correlation is sign(p')·ε = +0.18, yet the dashboard labels ε = −0.18 'Spot-vol correlation (leverage)'. Leverage appears only after about 1 day, through θ = 2.854, i.e. a −1.85 weight on the slow factor. The paper requires θ ≥ 0 and all its reported fits have θ ∈ [0.68, 0.96].

(5) θ sits at 95% of its upper bound (3.0) and the dashboard does not flag it; only ε saturation is flagged.
findings.evidence:
Scale invariance: with α scaled by 0.5, VIXfut(0.2329) = 25.82878 and the SPX IVs [0.25601, 0.25377, 0.23443] are identical to all printed digits.

Sign flip: α → −α gives the same VIXfut of 25.82878, but the SPX IVs become [0.01239, 0.00667, 0.00723].

Stored fit:
- roots of p': none real; p has a single real root at z = 0.5856
- P(p(Z_t) < 0) = 0.0597 for t ≥ 0.25
- E[max(p,0)²]/E[p²] = 0.998

From the paper: 'one can normalize the polynomial p(·) by any non-zero constant… We can thus fix α₅ = 1', and 'the underlying spot S is a true martingale whenever α₅ > 0 and ρ ≤ 0'.

The reference code applies no floor: volatility = f_func/sqrt(normal_var).
findings.proposed_fix:
1. Fix α5 = 1, leaving 7 free parameters as in the paper, or equivalently fix one other coefficient. Optionally add α2 and α4, since the paper's p has all degrees.
2. Remove the floor at quintic_ou.py:414. A signed σ is well defined in dS = Sσ dB, and it keeps SPX consistent with E[σ²] = ξ0 and with the VIX formula.
3. Restrict θ to [0, 1], or at least θ ≥ 0 with a warning when θ > 1.
4. Add boundary flags for every parameter.
5. Display the effective instantaneous correlation sign(p'(0))·ε instead of the raw ε.

Tests:
- loss(x) is not equal to loss(x with α scaled);
- MC E[σ_t²] matches ξ0(t) within 1% (this requires removing the floor);
- the calibrator rejects or warns on α5·ε > 0.

findings.title: The SPX calibration set has no skew (K/S from 0.994 to 1.071), and its target is vendor IV with conventions that do not match the calibrator's S, r and q
findings.description:
The calibrator selects the 9 highest-vega strikes per expiry, so every one of the 54 SPX quotes is within ±1–7% of spot and there is no OTM put. Skew, which is the whole point of the quintic map, is never constrained, and the dashboard's 'captures steep SPX left skew' is untested and in fact false.

The target is the vendor's `implied_vol`, while model IVs use the hard-coded r = 4.5%, q = 1.3% and the close S = 6556.37. The stored option mids imply S ≈ 6567.5 under those r and q. The mismatch between the vendor IVs and IVs inverted from the mids with the calibrator's own S, r and q is of the same order as the reported fit. `market_price_f` is computed at line 231 and never used.

The loss also silently drops model points that return NaN (valid mask, line 362). The optimizer can therefore improve the loss by pushing hard quotes into no-arbitrage failure. This happens today at K/S ≤ 0.90 (see the MC finding).
findings.evidence:
Calibration set: strikes 6520–7025 against S = 6556.37, i.e. K/S between 0.994 and 1.071. Only 7 of the 54 rows are puts, all with K/S ≥ 0.994.

Mid→IV with S=6556.37, r=4.5%, q=1.3%, minus the vendor IV: mean −0.54 vp, RMSE 1.57 vp, range [−2.70, +2.41]. At T=0.986: vendor 0.2229 vs mid-implied 0.1971.

Put-call parity on the 03-24 chain gives an implied spot of 6564–6570 across T from 0.036 to 0.986, not 6556.37.

Market put skew from K/S = 0.90 to ATM at T=0.4877 is +5.0 vp. The model gives −3.0 vp with the repo pricer and +1.0 vp with the correct Ito pricer.
findings.proposed_fix:
1. Choose strikes across a log-moneyness grid per expiry, e.g. k ∈ [−0.25, +0.05], in the spirit of the reference code's spx_lm_range_rule, weighted by vega. Do not take the top-9 by vega.
2. Derive the per-expiry forward from put-call parity and invert the market mids with Black-76 on that forward.
3. Use r from ^IRX, as the backtest already does, and drop the fixed q.
4. Fit in the same convention on both sides, or fit prices normalised by vega.
5. Penalise model failures (NaN) with a large fixed residual instead of dropping them.

Test: the chosen set spans K/F ≤ 0.9 for T ≥ 1M, and market IVs re-inverted with the calibrator's forward match their mids.

findings.title: The VIX leg takes 96% of each loss evaluation because of redundant scalar recomputation (about 900× headroom); the calibration objective uses 10×10 GH but reported numbers use 22×22
findings.description:
price_vix_option recomputes VIX² at every GH node for each strike, even though VIX² does not depend on K. compute_vix2 also recomputes the unconditional E[p(Z_s)²] for every GH node, although it depends only on s. Everything runs in scalar Python loops. The result is the '~46 min on 8 cores' calibration.

The objective is minimised with 10×10 GH and 16 Gauss–Legendre points, while calibrate() reports RMSE using 22×22 and 20. The published 17.5 vp is therefore not the value of the minimised objective, and GH on the kinked payoff is non-monotone (see the 80×80 vs 40×40 values in the evidence). The authors' code uses 1450-point optimal quantization with moment matching.
findings.evidence:
One _loss evaluation at the stored params: SPX leg 0.17 s, VIX-options leg 4.09 s.

A vectorised version (compute VIX² at the GH nodes once per expiry with the moment recurrence on arrays, then reuse it for the futures and all strikes) matches price_vix_futures/price_vix_option to a max abs diff of 7.1e-15, in 3.4 ms vs 3.04 s: an 895× speedup.

Quadrature at T=0.2329, K=23, model IV:
- 10×10: 0.8417
- 22×22: 0.8576
- 40×40: 0.8588
- 80×80: 0.8556

At T=0.0603, K=23: 1.4578 (10×10) vs 1.4666 (22×22).
findings.proposed_fix:
1. Add a function vix_at_nodes(T, params, fv, n_outer, n_inner) that returns (vix_values, weights) using the vectorised array moment recurrence. Price the futures and all strikes from it.
2. Cache ep_uncond(s) per s node.
3. Use the same quadrature for calibration and reporting, e.g. 24×24 GH, or a quantization grid with moment matching.
4. Re-state the fit time after the change.

Tests:
- the vectorised prices equal the current scalar prices to 1e-12;
- IV at 24×24 vs 48×48 differs by < 0.3 vp on a strike grid.

findings.title: QuinticCalibrator lacks the staleness and sufficiency guards added to JointCalibrator: VIX tenors from different dates, a months-old surface, no data gate
findings.description: _prepare_vix_term_structure takes row.iloc[-1] separately for each ticker from the full history up to as_of. When a sub-tenor is missing it silently mixes dates, which is the defect C20 fixed in JointCalibrator by pinning the leg to the spot session. _prepare_spx_surface neither records nor checks the snapshot_date, so as_of dates after the last snapshot calibrate a frozen surface against today's spot: the C21 bug, fixed only in the Heston path. There is no minimum-expiry or minimum-tenor gate, the same failure mode as the ongoing outage. Tenors are hard-coded as 91 and 182 days, while CBOE defines VIX3M as 93 days and VIX6M as 184 days and the DB stores tenor_days = 93. The effect of the tenors is negligible (the bootstrapped forward vol changes by less than 0.02 vp), but they should be read from the DB. The 2026-03-24 pickle is not affected.
findings.evidence:
QuinticCalibrator('2026-06-17').vix_ts gives [17.26, 18.44, 20.51, 22.59]. Here ^VIX = 18.44 is from 06-17, while ^VIX9D/^VIX3M/^VIX6M (17.26/20.51/22.59) are the 06-12 closes: the DB has NaN for those tickers on 06-15..06-17.

Quintic on '2026-09-23': S = 7500.58, SPX snapshot used = 2026-06-20, n_spx = 27, with no warning.

ξ0 with 91/182-day tenors: [28.21, 26.392, 26.366, 27.864] vol. With 93/184: [28.21, 26.392, 26.372, 27.878].

findings.title: MC step of 50/yr (minimum 10) with λx up to 500 and the same normal for the OU innovation and ΔW misrepresents the joint law. The reference code uses 252/yr (minimum 100)
findings.description: With λx = 168 and dt = 0.02, λx·dt is 3.4. The true correlation between the exact OU innovation and the Brownian increment over the step is (1−e^{−λdt})/λ/(sx√dt) = 0.75, but the code uses 1. Even with a correct left-point scheme, this makes IVs depend on the grid. The calibrated parameters then absorb the grid error. The upper bound λx = 500 makes this worse.
findings.evidence:
Left-point scheme with shared Z1, overall RMSE vs market: 3.964 vp at 50 steps/yr vs 4.179 vp at 2520 steps/yr. Per-expiry mean IV:
- T=0.488: 0.2566 vs 0.2626
- T=0.986: 0.2646 vs 0.2695

With an exact joint (I_X, I_Y, ΔW) Gaussian step, IV at T=0.986, K=6925 is 0.2669 / 0.2676 / 0.2677 for 50 / 252 / 1000 steps/yr.
findings.proposed_fix:
Use the exact 3-D Gaussian step described in the anticipating-scheme finding, with n_steps = max(100, round(252·T)).

Test: IV change between 252 and 1000 steps/yr < 0.3 vp at the calibrated params.

findings.title: Both paper citations in the model header are attributed to the wrong authors
findings.description: arXiv:2503.14158 is by Abi Jaber & Li, not 'Bourgey & de Marco (2025)'. arXiv:2212.10917 is by Abi Jaber, Illand & Li, not 'Carr, Pelts & Tehranchi (2022)'. The calibrator cites a 'Bourgey–de Marco (2025) calibration design'. The 'two-factor' label itself is accurate for 2503.14158. The code's odd-plus-constant polynomial with free α5 matches neither paper exactly: 2503.14158 uses a full degree-5 p with α5 = 1, and Section 3.2 uses odd terms with α5 = 1. Docstrings also disagree on the range of ε: line 32 says (−1, 0) and line 65 says (−1, 1).
findings.evidence:
arxiv.org/abs/2503.14158: 'Capturing Smile Dynamics with the Quintic Volatility Model: SPX, Skew-Stickiness Ratio and VIX', Eduardo Abi Jaber and Shaun (Xiaoyuan) Li.

arxiv.org/abs/2212.10917: 'The quintic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck volatility model that jointly calibrates SPX & VIX smiles', Abi Jaber, Illand, Li.

grep finds 'Bourgey' and 'Pelts' only in these two files.
findings.proposed_fix: Correct the author lists and titles. State which paper variant is implemented (two-factor, odd polynomial) and link the authors' reference implementation. Make the ε docstrings agree with the bounds.

findings.title: The quintic tests are too weak to catch these bugs: no martingale test, a broken antithetic test, a misnamed monotonicity test, and no calibrator coverage
findings.description:
Problems in the test file:
- The header claims 30 tests; there are 36.
- test_vix2_increases_with_xt asserts only that values are positive.
- test_antithetic_reduces_std_err never compares against plain MC; its threshold is 20 while its comment says 10, so it passes with the broken antithetics.
- test_cond_var_Z_equals_var_Z_of_dt is tautological, because _cond_var_Z literally returns var_Z.
- Nothing checks E[S_T] = F, VIX² against brute-force MC, E[σ²] = ξ0 under the MC, Jensen (E[VIX] ≤ forward VIX), or put-call parity.
- quintic_calibrator.py (_PiecewiseConstVar, _spot_vix, the data preparation, the loss) has zero test references.
findings.evidence:
`grep -c 'def test_'` gives 36. `pytest test_quintic_ou.py`: 36 passed in 0.82 s. `grep -rl quintic_calibrator joint_vol_calibration/tests` returns nothing.

The fixture params fail a martingale check: E[S_T/F] = 0.96318 ± 0.00043 at T = 1.

My brute-force conditional MC validates compute_vix2: 411.81 ± 0.05 vs 411.86. That test is cheap to add.

findings.title: Quintic panel shows MC and quadrature settings the code does not use, and hides that the fit did not converge
findings.description: The panel says 'MC paths: 6,000/expiry'; the code uses 5,000 in calibration and 10,000 in the final evaluation. It says 'VIX quad: 18² = 324 pts'; the code uses 10² = 100 in calibration and 22² = 484 in reporting, while the same panel's header says '≈ 500 pts'. The stored pickle has success = False (DE stopped at maxiter = 40 without converging), and the panel does not show it. The half-life is labelled 'd' while computed as ln2/λ·252, i.e. trading days on a calendar-year λ.
findings.evidence:
Live page text: 'MC paths: 6,000/expiry VIX quad: 18² = 324 pts'.

quintic_calibrator.py:55-58: _MC_PATHS_CAL = 5_000, _VIX_QUAD_OUTER = 10. Lines 489 and 513-517 use n_paths = 10,000 and the default 22×22.

Pickle: 'success': False, 'n_evals': 2813 (64×41 DE + 189 L-BFGS).
findings.proposed_fix:
Render these settings from values stored in the pickle (n_paths, quadrature, seed, success) instead of literals, add a 'not converged' badge, and label the half-life 'trading days'.

Test: a template test asserting that the displayed settings equal the pickle's metadata.

findings.title: Quintic and Bates pickles lack provenance, so the published numbers are reproducible only while the DB and code stay unchanged
findings.description: The result dict stores only params, loss, leg RMSEs, time, evals and success. It omits S, r, q, the ξ0 nodes, the snapshot date, seed, n_paths, the quadrature, the code SHA and the per-option market/model arrays. The S question can only be settled by trial: the fit reproduces only with S = 6556.37, while the Heston baseline used 6581.0. Pickling a dataclass also ties the file to the module path. The Bates pickle stores n_evals = 0, which is wrong (_n_evals is reset and the DE workers' counts are lost).
findings.evidence:
Reproduced SPX 2.3427 vp with S = 6556.37 (2.3740 with S = 6581.0), VIX futures 0.001147 and VIX options 17.5297 exactly. That match was possible only because the snapshot and code are unchanged.

Bates pickle: 'n_evals': 0 with fit_time 139 s.
findings.proposed_fix:
Save a versioned JSON sidecar containing params (as a dict), S, r, q, xi0 t_nodes/xi_nodes, snapshot dates, seeds, MC and quadrature settings, git SHA, and the per-option (T, K, right, market_iv, model_iv) rows. Take n_evals from the nfev values.

Test: reload the file and recompute the leg RMSEs within 1e-6.

findings.title: The fallback forward-variance curve uses average (term) variance as forward variance
findings.description: When the VIX term structure is missing, ξ0 on (T_{i−1}, T_i] is set to σ_ATM(T_i)², which is the average variance to T_i. The forward variance is (σ_i²T_i − σ_{i−1}²T_{i−1})/(T_i − T_{i−1}), which the primary path correctly bootstraps. The fallback therefore does not reproduce its own input term structure.
findings.evidence: Mini-repro: with ATM IV 0.15 at T=0.1 and 0.25 at T=0.5, the fallback gives xi_nodes [0.0225, 0.0625], and _spot_vix(0.5) = 23.35 instead of 25.0. The correct ξ on (0.1, 0.5] is 0.0725, i.e. 26.9% vol.
findings.proposed_fix:
Apply the same cumulative-variance bootstrap used for the VIX path to the ATM total variances, with a floor on negative forwards.

Test: _spot_vix(T_i) reproduces each input ATM vol within 0.01.

checked_ok: Model description: 'two-factor' is accurate. arXiv:2503.14158 (Abi Jaber & Li) defines Z = θX + (1−θ)Y with two OU processes driven by the same Brownian motion, σ = g0(t)p(Z) and g0² = ξ0/E[p(Z_t)²]; the code implements this (odd-plus-constant p).
The Gaussian moment recurrence E[Z^n] = μE[Z^{n−1}] + (n−1)σ²E[Z^{n−2}] is correct. ep_squared matches 200-point Gauss–Hermite quadrature to 5 digits (0.18277 vs 0.18277; 0.23315 vs 0.23315).

var_Z and the conditional variance are correct for OU processes with a common Brownian motion and X0 = Y0 = 0. The conditional law Z_s | F_T ~ N(θx e^{−λx(s−T)} + (1−θ)y e^{−λy(s−T)}, var_Z(s−T)) matches the paper.
g0 normalisation: g0² · E[p(Z_t)²] = ξ0(t) holds exactly. With the floor, the MC variance loss at the optimum is only 0.2% (E[max(p,0)²]/E[p²] = 0.998).

compute_vix2 formula VIX² = (100²/Δ) ∫ ξ0(s) E[p²|F_T]/E[p²] ds with Δ = 30/365 is correct. Validated against a brute-force conditional MC (200k paths, exact joint OU steps): 411.81 ± 0.05 vs 411.86 (smooth ξ0). Gauss–Legendre error across the real ξ0 jumps is ≤ 0.14% in VIX (T = 0.2329: 25.4831 at n=16 vs 25.5188 at n=400).
The 2-D Gauss–Hermite construction (√2 node scaling, weights normalised by π, Cholesky of the (X_T, Y_T) covariance) is correct. VIX futures converge at 10×10 (25.829 vs 25.854 at 80×80).
_PiecewiseConstVar step convention (side='left' puts ξ on (t_{i−1}, t_i]) and the VIX-term-structure bootstrap reproduce the input index levels: 26.9500 vs 26.95, 26.562 vs 26.56, 27.221 vs 27.22.
The stored pickle is reproducible with current code and DB at S = 6556.37: SPX 2.3427 vp, VIX futures 0.001147, VIX options 17.5297 vp, loss 0.0092549859 (matches the stored 0.0092549859007).
Units are consistent: VIX² is in index points², IV RMSEs are ×100 into vol points, VIX strikes are in index points, and futures RMSE is in index points.

CRN seeding (seed + 1 per expiry, fixed across evaluations) is deterministic, and the stored n_evals of 2813 = 64×41 DE + 189 L-BFGS is consistent. The DE worker setup (picklable objective, updating='deferred') is correct.
The 03-24 inputs are all dated 03-24 (options snapshot 2026-03-24, all four VIX tenors present on 2026-03-24), so the stored pickle itself has no look-ahead or date mixing.
